significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that the per-fact "minimal ablation-set size = redundancy" increases with reliability or frequency and predictively couples to both post-edit recovery and activation-noise tolerance; this is a form-(iii) law relating measurable quantities, not merely an existence claim. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—robust facts resist editing and noise—and a mechanism in which "multiple independent loci" suffice for recall, fixing expectations for interventions beyond the facts used to derive the count; this bears directly on the mismatch between causal localization and effective editing documented around ROME, MEMIT, and Hase et al.'s Does Localization Inform Editing? (NeurIPS 2023). The branches are determinate: failure of these couplings would reject redundancy count as the proposed unifying explanation, although it would not rule out every distributed-storage account. After topic substitution, the score falls substantially because the generic topic asks only whether knowledge is localized or distributed, whereas this claim adds a graded quantity and three directional predictions, so the importance is claim-specific rather than inherited from the topic.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the claimed "redundancy count," specifically the "minimal ablation-set size," offered as a "diagnostic for which facts are safely editable and which will resist editing." It provides ex-ante lead time for model editing because the count is asserted to predict edit resistance before an edit is selected or deployed, while its use for explaining noise tolerance is primarily diagnostic. Although the quantity must be re-extracted on each model, the conclusion predicts what the recalibrated count should imply—greater redundancy means greater edit resistance and noise robustness—so a relation, not merely a search procedure, survives recalibration; the asserted scope is "across models and a large fact set," with model-editing researchers and practitioners as downstream users. Topic substitution would not retain this score because the broad knowledge-representation topic supplies neither this screening quantity nor its predictive rule, though the absence of a stronger architecture- or training-invariant law limits the reach below the top band.
